question: What is the main job of hemostasis in the body?

options.A: To make more white blood cells quickly
options.B: To keep blood pressure high during stress
options.C: To break down old red blood cells
options.D: To stop bleeding when a blood vessel gets injured

explanation: You've got this! Hemostasis is simply the body's natural way of stopping blood loss from a damaged vessel while keeping the rest of the blood flowing smoothly. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h1)

question: What happens if the body's clotting system becomes overly active?

options.B: Blood clots form inside healthy blood vessels
options.D: Severe bleeding occurs all over the body

explanation: Great try! When the balance tips too much toward clotting, abnormal blood clots can form where they shouldn't be, right inside normal, healthy vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the very first thing that happens when a small blood vessel is cut?

options.B: White blood cells rush to the area
options.C: The blood vessel spasms and narrows

explanation: Think of the vessel like a smart pipe—it tightens up instantly to slow down blood flow right after an injury, even before the actual clotting factors kick in! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why is the first platelet plug considered weak on its own?

options.A: It dissolves when exposed to air
options.B: It gets washed away by white blood cells
options.C: It lacks a strong meshwork of fibrin
options.D: It depends entirely on red blood cells

explanation: You're doing great! A temporary platelet plug is like a loose pile of sand; it needs sticky fibrin fibers woven through it to lock it tightly in place. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h2)

question: What gets the extrinsic pathway of blood clotting started?

options.A: Massive destruction of red blood cells
options.B: Direct contact of factor XII with collagen
options.C: Release of tissue factor from damaged tissues outside the vessel
options.D: Spontaneous activation of fibrinogen in the blood

explanation: Think 'extrinsic' as external! When tissue outside a broken vessel gets damaged, it releases tissue factor to quickly sound the alarm for a fast clot. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h3)

question: How is the intrinsic pathway different from the extrinsic pathway?

options.A: It relies entirely on clotting factors already floating inside the blood
options.C: It doesn't use any chemical signals
options.D: It is only triggered by outer tissue damage

explanation: You're learning fast! 'Intrinsic' means internal—these clotting factors are already circulating in the blood, ready to react when the inner lining of a vessel is damaged. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the main job of thrombin during blood clotting?

options.A: Releasing tissue factor from smooth muscle
options.B: Converting soluble fibrinogen into solid fibrin strands
options.D: Stopping too many platelets from clumping

explanation: Thrombin is a star player! It acts as an enzyme that turns loose, dissolved fibrinogen into strong, sturdy fibrin threads to build a solid clot. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the specific job of factor XIII in the clotting process?

options.A: Destroying extra platelets to clear vessels
options.B: Cross-linking fibrin strands to make the clot strong and stable
options.D: Starting the extrinsic pathway after an injury

explanation: Spot on! Factor XIII acts like glue, cross-linking the fibrin threads so the blood clot becomes tough and durable enough to withstand blood pressure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which enzyme is responsible for breaking down blood clots when healing is done?
explanation: You've got this! Plasmin is the body's cleanup crew enzyme that safely digests and dissolves the old fibrin mesh once the blood vessel has healed. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h5)

question: What does clot retraction do to help a healing wound?

options.A: Stops any more platelets from gathering
options.B: Pulls the broken edges of the blood vessel closer together
options.C: Quickly raises blood pressure in the tissue

explanation: Brilliant! As the clot shrinks, it pulls the sides of the broken vessel together, making it much easier for the tissue to repair itself. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which substance does antithrombin III mainly neutralize to stop extra clotting?
explanation: Antithrombin III is a great bodyguard for your blood vessels—it grabs onto thrombin and stops it from making unnecessary clots! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h6)

question: How do healthy, undamaged blood vessel linings prevent unwanted clots?

options.B: By releasing active thrombin into the blood
options.C: By releasing substances like prostacyclin to keep platelets calm
options.D: By turning on the intrinsic pathway during rest

explanation: Healthy vessels are super smart. They release calming chemicals like prostacyclin so platelets just float right past without sticking or causing trouble. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which lab test is used to monitor a patient taking the drug warfarin?
explanation: Remember, warfarin affects the extrinsic pathway, and we monitor it using the Prothrombin Time, commonly reported as an INR value. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h7)

question: A patient receiving a continuous IV heparin infusion needs which lab test monitored?
explanation: You're doing great! Heparin works mainly on the intrinsic pathway, which is checked and tracked using the aPTT lab test. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h7)

question: Hemophilia A is caused by a shortage of which specific clotting factor?
explanation: Hemophilia A is a well-known inherited condition where the body lacks enough Factor VIII, making it harder for blood to clot normally. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why does Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) strangely lead to severe bleeding?

options.A: Massive red blood cell breakdown destroys blood vessels
options.B: Widespread small clots use up all available platelets and clotting factors
options.C: Platelets actively destroy all circulating fibrinogen
options.D: The liver completely stops making plasma proteins

explanation: DIC is tricky—it causes tiny clots all over the body first, which completely uses up all the clotting supplies, leaving none left when a real bleed happens! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h8)
